title: Mass-imbalanced SU(N) Fermi gases
authors: Jordi Pera, Joaquim Casulleras, Jordi Boronat
abstract: We report a fully analytical description of zero-temperature itinerant ferromagnetism in repulsive SU(N) Fermi gases with arbitrary mass imbalance among components. Using perturbation theory in the gas parameter x = kFa0, with kF the Fermi momentum and a0 the s-wave scattering length, we derive the second-order energy for arbitrary spin polarization and arbitrary mass ratio. Our main result is a closed analytic expression for the beyond-mean-field correction in mixtures with unequal masses. This analytical result extends the theory of dilute Fermi gases beyond the mass-balanced case and provides a compact equation of state for multicomponent mixtures. We show that mass imbalance breaks the paramagnetic symmetry already in the non-interacting limit, favors the occu pation of heavier components, and lowers the interaction strength required to reach a fully polarized state. For S = 1/2, the system evolves continuously from a mass-induced partially polarized state to full ferromagnetism. For larger spins, distinct mass distributions generate qualitatively differ ent polarization paths, including smooth and discontinuous sequences. Our results identify mass imbalance as a powerful control tool for magnetic ordering in ultracold Fermi mixtures.
summary: This paper analytically describes itinerant ferromagnetism in mass-imbalanced SU(N) Fermi gases by calculating the second-order energy corrections. The key finding is that mass imbalance fundamentally changes the magnetic transition path, leading to continuous polarization rather than a sharp discontinuity seen in balanced systems. This establishes mass ratio as a powerful control parameter for magnetism in ultracold atomic mixtures.
main_problem: The study focuses on developing a fully analytical description of itinerant ferromagnetism in repulsive SU(N) Fermi gases, specifically investigating how mass imbalance among components affects the magnetic ordering.
main_result: Mass imbalance fundamentally alters the path to full polarization, causing it to occur continuously (for S=1/2) rather than discontinuously as predicted for equal-mass systems. The derived analytical expression provides a compact equation of state for these mixtures.
method: The authors employ perturbation theory up to second order in the gas parameter $x = k_F a_0$ to derive the energy and beyond-mean-field corrections, yielding closed analytical expressions previously unavailable for mass-imbalanced cases.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a zero-temperature, repulsive SU(N) Fermi gas characterized by arbitrary mass imbalance among its components. The physics is governed by interactions quantified by the s-wave scattering length $a_0$.
key_observables: Energy per particle ($E_N$), spin polarization (P), and occupation factors of different spin components.
important_parameters: The gas parameter ($x = k_F a_0$), the degree of mass imbalance (quantified by ratios $r_\lambda$), and the total spin degeneracy ($S$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to zero temperature, repulsive short-range interactions ($a_0 > 0$), and relies on perturbation theory up to second order.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy dependence on $x$ for mass-balanced versus imbalanced systems (Fig. 1). They also show how mass asymmetry leads to continuous polarization paths (Fig. 2) and plot the critical gas parameter required for full polarization as a function of maximum mass ratio (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the physical model (mass-imbalanced SU(N) Fermi gases) to deriving the second-order energy correction analytically. It then analyzes how this imbalance breaks symmetry, favors heavier components, and modifies the transition dynamics toward ferromagnetism across different spin values.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical tool—'mass engineering'—to control magnetic ordering in ultracold atomic mixtures, offering quantitative predictions that guide experimental realization using heterogeneous quantum gases.
